components.css: .ds-stack{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;display:flex;flex-direction:column-reverse;gap:3px;width:280px;background:var(--k0,oklch(0.155 0.008 65));padding:12px}.ds-cab{display:flex;align-items:flex-end;justify-content:space-between;gap:8px;width:100%;padding:4px 10px;border:0;border-radius:4px;background-color:oklch(var(--l) 0.12 var(--h));background-image:radial-gradient(oklch(0 0 0 / 0.32) 1px,transparent 1.4px);background-size:4px 4px;box-shadow:inset 0 -2px 0 oklch(0 0 0 / 0.25),inset 0 1px 0 oklch(1 0 0 / 0.08);color:oklch(0.97 0.03 var(--h));font-family:'Big Shoulders Stencil',sans-serif;font-weight:800;line-height:1;text-shadow:0 1px 0 oklch(0 0 0 / 0.35);cursor:pointer;transition:height 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1),filter 120ms;overflow:hidden}.ds-cab:hover{filter:brightness(1.12)}.ds-cab:focus-visible{outline:2px solid oklch(0.85 0.17 92);outline-offset:2px}.ds-cab[aria-pressed=true]{outline:2px solid oklch(0.955 0.01 85);outline-offset:2px;filter:brightness(1.18)}.ds-cab-row{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px}.ds-cab-row.short .ds-cab{flex:0 0 62%}.ds-aside{font-family:'Big Shoulders Stencil',sans-serif;font-weight:800;font-size:15px;line-height:1;color:oklch(0.85 0.08 var(--h))}

narrative.overview:
The library is a UK bass-culture speaker stack. Every proposed playlist is a cabinet: a matte, grille-dotted face in its own hue, stencilled with its name and song count, stacked bottom-up with the biggest at the base. The stack is a measuring instrument before it is a picture: a cabinet's height is its song count times one fixed unit, so the visitor sizes up their own music at a glance and opens a cabinet to see what is inside.

Everything around the stack is a working tool in warm plywood black: a left rail of five steps, a stage with the stack beside the open cabinet's track list, and a player bar along the bottom. The surround is quiet on purpose: one seven-step neutral ramp, one hazard yellow that only ever means "do this", and Figtree for every word that is not painted on a cabinet. Density is that of a tool, not a poster: 15px body, tabular numerals, rows rather than cards.

The world refuses the category default of a grey sidebar, a green accent and a flat table of playlists, and it never imitates Spotify's branding or logo.
keyCharacteristics: Warm matte black surround built from exactly seven neutral steps.
Hazard yellow is the action colour and nothing else.
One OKLCH hue per playlist, tinting its cabinet, chips, swatches and heading.
Stencil lettering only where a label is painted on equipment: cabinets, counts, the list heading, big numbers, the wordmark.
Cabinet height exactly proportional to song count; motion is a height step and nothing else.

rules.name: The Seven Steps Rule
rules.body: The k0–k6 ramp is the only neutral set. A new grey is a new step nobody agreed to; use the nearest of the seven.

rules.name: The Hazard Rule
rules.body: Hazard yellow marks what to do next: the primary action, focus, the caret, the current step. It is never a decoration, a playlist colour or a status tint.

rules.name: The Reserved Yellows Rule
rules.body: OKLCH hues 60–130 (yellows and yellow-greens) never go on a playlist, so no cabinet can be mistaken for a button.

rules.name: The Fixed Colour Rule
rules.body: A playlist keeps its colour for the whole session. Colours are assigned in rule order, not stack position, and once shown they are held, so re-sorting the stack never repaints a cabinet. When a playlist's preferred colour family (hues within 40°) is taken, it moves to the free slot furthest from the rest.

rules.name: The Painted-On Rule
rules.body: Stencil appears only where a label would be painted onto equipment: cabinet names and counts, the open cabinet's heading, big numbers, the wordmark. Body copy, buttons, rail steps and track titles are always Figtree.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Numerals are tabular throughout (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on body), so counts and timers do not jitter as they change.

rules.name: The Exact Height Rule
rules.body: A cabinet's face is songs × unit pixels, never rounded for looks. The unit is 560 / total songs, clamped to 2–8px (halved in compact stacks). When a face is shorter than 22px, its label moves beside the cabinet (the face shrinks to 62% width) rather than the cabinet growing to fit it.

rules.name: The Grille Rule
rules.body: The grille-dot texture (radial-gradient(oklch(0 0 0 / 0.32) 1px, transparent 1.4px) at 4px × 4px) appears only on cabinet faces. Nothing else in the app has texture.

dos: Do take every neutral from the k0–k6 ramp and every playlist colour from the OKLCH [hue, lightness] palette.
Do keep hazard yellow for the one primary action, focus, caret and current step.
Do size cabinets exactly by song count (`songs × unit`) and move the label beside any face under 22px.
Do keep a playlist's colour fixed for the session, assigned in rule order.
Do set cabinet names, counts, the open-cabinet heading and big numbers in Big Shoulders Stencil 800; everything else in Figtree with tabular numerals.
Do snap spacing to the 4px grid (4–32px).
Do animate only height steps (160ms ease-out) and honour reduced motion with instant changes.
Do keep removed songs visible, struck through and restorable.
donts: Don't give a playlist a hue between 60 and 130; those yellows belong to actions.
Don't use hazard yellow as decoration, a playlist colour or a status tint.
Don't put the grille texture or the cabinet bevel on anything but a cabinet face.
Don't set buttons, body copy, rail steps or track titles in the stencil face.
Don't fade content in or out, or animate anything other than a cabinet's height.
Don't round cabinet heights up for looks or give short cabinets a minimum height.
Don't imitate Spotify's green, logo or branding, and don't fall back to a grey sidebar with a flat playlist table.
Don't use drop shadows for elevation; step up the black ramp instead.
openIssues: With more than about seven playlists in one stack, some cabinets can share a colour family: outside the reserved yellows the palette holds about nine distinguishable families (12 slots, several within 40° of each other), so the fallback picks the furthest free slot rather than a distinct family.
